text:
Timo Meier is shooting like a 30-goal winger and scoring like a third-liner, and that gap is starting to close. He has 83 shots in 22 games, the kind of volume few forwards match, but only 5 goals on 8.5 expected, so our numbers list him as due. Lately the pucks have started to go: two against Toronto, a power-play goal against Washington, and a breakaway finish past Jakob Fowler in the 3-2 loss to Montreal on Nov. 19. Mike Fink of The Hockey News asked the question on everyone's mind in New Jersey: "Timo Time?"

The process has been there all along. The Devils get about 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile for chances from right in front of the net last season, and Evolving-Hockey put his play-driving impact in the 88th percentile, even as his overall value came in low.

He's 30, with 241 career goals before this season. Watch the conversion over the next few weeks. Players with this many good looks rarely stay this far behind them.
